transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I just have a hard time sitting still. Like if I'm stuck in a staff meeting at work, or... church event briefings. 

I just get this feeling like... like there's a motor humming under my skin. I usually end up shifting around a lot, or I just find some excuse to stand up and move. So... yeah. That's it, really.
Do you also notice any uncomfortable sensations in your legs, like crawling, tingling, or aching, especially when you're trying to sit still or rest?
No... I haven't noticed anything like that. Um, no tingling or crawling. Just... just what I said before. I just need to get up.
Do you feel the need to move mostly when you're trying to stay still, like when you're relaxing or trying to rest, or does it happen more when you're already active?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really kept track of it like that. 

I guess I just always sort of feel it. I don't know if it's worse when I'm resting or not. I just... I don't really know.
Do you feel a sense of inner restlessness or discomfort that makes it really hard to stay still, and does moving around help you feel better?

Um... I wouldn't really call it discomfort. I just... I don't know. 

I'm used to being on my feet a lot for work, so sitting just feels... I don't really know how to describe it. I haven't really thought about whether moving makes me feel better. I just do it.
When you feel the need to move, does it tend to happen more when you're trying to rest or relax, and does moving around actually make the feeling go away or feel better?

I... I think that's kind of what you just asked me. Like I said, I don't really know. 

I don't keep track of whether I'm trying to relax when it happens. And I don't know if moving makes anything go away. I just move. That's... that's really all I can tell you about it.
Can you tell me if this feeling that makes you move is accompanied by a sense of inner agitation or mental restlessness, like you just can’t settle down inside?

I don't really know about... inner agitation. I don't think about it like that. I'm just... I'm just a guy who moves around a lot. I don't really sit there and analyze how my mind feels when I'm doing it.
Do you ever notice any movements that happen without you meaning to, like twitching or jerking, especially when you're not trying to move?
No, I... I haven't noticed anything like that. No twitching or jerking. Just regular moving.
Do you ever notice any unusual movements in your legs or arms when you're falling asleep or while you're sleeping?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I'm asleep, so I wouldn't really know. But nobody's ever told me I do that.
Do you find it especially hard to stay seated in situations where you're expected to, like during meetings or meals, and do you ever feel like you just have to get up even if it's inconvenient?

Yeah... I guess so. If I'm supposed to just sit still, like in staff meetings or... church event briefings, it's tough. I just get this feeling like there's a motor humming under my skin. I usually end up shifting around a lot, or... I'll just stand up in the back. Or I find some excuse to go check on something so I can move around.
When you feel the need to move, is it mostly your legs that feel like they need to move, like there’s something uncomfortable in them that makes you want to shift or stand up?
No... not really. It's not just my legs. And they don't feel uncomfortable or weird or anything like that. I just... I just prefer to be on my feet.
Do you notice that this feeling in your body, the need to move, is worse during the evening or at night compared to during the day?
No... I wouldn't say that. It's pretty much just the same during the day. Night doesn't really make a difference.
Do you ever notice any shaking or trembling in your hands or other parts of your body, especially when you're trying to do something like holding a cup or writing?
No. I don't really have any shaking. My hands are fine.
When you feel like moving, is it because you sense something uncomfortable in your body that makes you want to shift or stand up, or do you just feel like moving even if your body feels fine?
It feels fine. There's no... uncomfortable feeling or anything like that. I just want to move.

When you're sitting or trying to relax, do you get a strong urge to move your legs specifically, like there's something pulling or tugging in them, and does moving your legs make that feeling go away?
No. I haven't noticed anything tugging. My legs are fine... it's not like that.
When you're lying down or sitting for a long time, like watching TV or trying to relax, do you get a strong, almost irresistible urge to move your legs, even if there's no pain or discomfort?
No, not really. I don't... it's not an urge like that. Like I said before, they're fine.
When you're in a situation where you need to sit still for a while, like watching TV or in a meeting, do you feel like you just can't stay seated even if there's no real reason for you to get up?

Yeah, I guess so. It's just... whenever I'm supposed to sit still, like at staff meetings or briefings for church events, I get this feeling. It's like... I don't know, like a motor humming under my skin. I just end up shifting around, or standing up, or finding some excuse to go do something else.
Do you ever find yourself making the same movements over and over again without meaning to, like rocking, tapping, or pacing?
No, not really. I don't... I don't think I do that. Just the shifting around, like I said.

When you're in a situation where you have to sit still, like watching TV or in a meeting, does it feel like you can't stay seated because of a restless, almost urgent need to move, even if your body doesn't feel uncomfortable?
I thought I just answered that. It's... it's just like I said. The motor feeling. I just can't sit still for long.
When you feel the need to move, is it mostly because you feel restless inside, even if your body feels okay?

Yeah... like I keep saying. It's inside. That motor humming feeling. My body doesn't hurt or anything, I just... I get restless and have to find an excuse to move around. I don't really know how else to explain it to you.
